text:
The EU AI Act entered into force in phases between 2024 and 2027 as a deliberate strategy to ensure that regulatory obligations land only after institutional capacity and technology have matured [Source: ev-1]. This phased schedule also serves as the compliance roadmap for the "Brussels effect," which is exported to providers worldwide [Source: ev-1]. The law was published on 2024-07-12 and officially entered into force on 2024/08/01 [Source: ev-1].

The different deadlines require specific actions based on risk tiers and system categories:
*   **Prohibited Practices ("Unacceptable Risk"):** These apply from 2025-02-02, requiring a cessation of banned activities such as social scoring and certain manipulative or exploitation-of-vulnerability uses [Source: ev-1].
*   **General-Purpose AI (GPAI) Models:** Obligations for these models begin on 2025/08/02. These duties are scaled by systemic-risk status, specifically referencing a threshold of $10^{26}$ FLOPs [Source: ev-1]. A GPAI Code of Practice was drafted through the period 2024–2025 with broad industry participation to interpret these obligations [Source: ev-1].
*   **High-Risk Systems:** Obligations apply from 2026/08/02, with a specific subset applying later from 2027-08-02 [Source: ev-1].

To enforce compliance, the Act establishes significant fines for non-compliance. Violations of prohibited practices can result in fines reaching €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover (whichever is higher), while most other breaches carry fines of up to €15 million or 3% [Source: ev-1]. Implementation is led by the European AI Office, which was established in 2024 in Brussels [Source: ev-1].
